q: What changed in SEBI's BRSR Core rules between July 2023 and March 2025?
title: BRSR Core: 2023 rules vs 2025 rules
short: Four things changed. Assessment is now allowed instead of reasonable assurance. Value chain partners are those at 2% or more of purchases or sales, not the top 75% cumulatively. Value chain reporting moved from comply-or-explain in FY 2024-25 to voluntary from FY 2025-26. A green credits line was added.
audience: Listed company ESG teams and their suppliers

ul: Verification of BRSR Core: 2023 said reasonable assurance; 2025 says assessment or assurance, with assessment done to Industry Standards Forum standards.
Who is a value chain partner: 2023 said top partners cumulatively making up 75% of purchases or sales; 2025 says partners that individually make up 2% or more, and coverage may stop at 75%.
Value chain disclosure: 2023 said top 250, comply-or-explain from FY 2024-25; 2025 says top 250, voluntary from FY 2025-26.
Value chain verification: 2023 said limited assurance, comply-or-explain from FY 2025-26; 2025 says assessment or assurance, voluntary from FY 2026-27.
Green credits: none in 2023; 2025 adds a Principle 6 leadership indicator from FY 2024-25.

p: The glide path for the listed company itself is the same: top 150 for FY 2023-24, top 250 for FY 2024-25, top 500 for FY 2025-26 and top 1,000 for FY 2026-27. The conflict of interest rule for the provider also stayed, now worded for assessment or assurance.

ul: In the first year of value chain reporting, prior year figures are voluntary.
A company that reports value chain data must state what share of its purchases and sales the covered partners represent.

senseible: Senseible turns a supplier's electricity bills and fuel invoices into Scope 1 and 2 figures for the financial year, with each bill linked to its line, so a customer's questionnaire can be answered from records. Figures are self-declared.
